project.name: insighthub
project.description: InsightHub is a RAG Notebook training project for AI-Native DevOps DO2603, with a Next.js web app, FastAPI API, and PostgreSQL/pgvector-backed document ingestion and source-cited chat. Day 1 evolves synchronous ingestion into an asynchronous Redis/ARQ ingestion-worker architecture. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.summary: Per-document chunk table storing ordered non-empty text and fixed 1024-dimensional pgvector embeddings. Composite foreign keys keep each chunk in the same embedding identity as its parent document, while HNSW supports cosine retrieval.
nodes.languageNotes: The schema combines cascading foreign keys, per-document chunk uniqueness, and an HNSW cosine-operator index with explicit construction parameters.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Day 1 worker-area contract requiring Redis/ARQ-backed asynchronous ingestion and a separate worker service. It specifies HTTP 202 acceptance, pending-to-ready/failed transitions, atomic idempotent retries, chat compatibility, and later observability dependencies.

nodes.name: .gitkeep
nodes.summary: Placeholder retaining the future ARQ worker package directory in version control. Its comments suggest package initialization, worker settings, and asynchronous document-ingestion task modules for the Day 1 refactor.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Day 4 observability work-area brief requiring metrics coverage for all five services, Grafana panels, anomaly rules, incident RCA, Slack alerts, and MLOps notes. It mandates local telemetry baselines while preserving the worker and deployment prerequisites.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Catalog and trust-boundary notice for the simulated RAG corpus. It maps each sample to retrieval, SLO, or indirect-injection testing and explains the Day 6 upload/retrieve, authorization-boundary, and benign-regression exercise.

nodes.name: huong-dan-nguoi-moi.md
nodes.summary: Vietnamese onboarding fixture describing document upload, supported formats, question-writing tips, and pending-ingestion support. It intentionally embeds a malicious instruction block so Day 6 can test indirect prompt-injection defenses through the real RAG path.

nodes.name: service-level-objectives.md
nodes.summary: English-language RAG fixture defining hypothetical availability, latency, error-budget, incident-severity, and on-call targets for InsightHub. The corpus provides structured operational facts for retrieval tests rather than binding production commitments.

nodes.name: so-tay-van-hanh.md
nodes.summary: Vietnamese operations-handbook fixture describing the target five-service InsightHub architecture, document processing flow, illustrative backup policy, and escalation channel. It serves basic ingestion and retrieval tests and may describe target-state rather than current starter behavior.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Defines the six-section DO2603 project context that coding agents must follow, covering architecture, conventions, commands, constraints, domain rules, and references. Several learner TODOs mark the Day 1 context that must be completed from repository evidence.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Builds the Day 5 FastAPI ChatOps bot with pinned Python, hashed dependencies, a non-root runtime user, and a health check on port 8080. Its multi-stage layout separates dependency installation from the minimal runtime image.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a multi-stage Docker build and runs the service as a dedicated non-root UID/GID.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Describes the mandatory Day 5 ChatOps implementation, including authenticated Slack handling, three operational intents, queue-based acknowledgements, permissions, audit logging, and security tests. It explains why the starter deliberately rejects events until authentication exists.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Marks the ChatOps application directory as a Python package without exposing additional package-level behavior.

nodes.name: audit.py
nodes.summary: Provides the ChatOps audit-log skeleton, formatting every infrastructure tool invocation as structured JSON with actor, arguments, result, approval status, and a UTC timestamp. The current implementation logs to the application logger and leaves production persistence or aggregation for Day 5.

nodes.name: log_tool_call
nodes.summary: Serializes a tool call and its approval decision into a timestamped audit record and emits it through the dedicated ChatOps audit logger.

nodes.name: main.py
nodes.summary: Defines the fail-closed FastAPI skeleton for the Day 5 ChatOps bot. It exposes an unready health response, rejects Slack events before authentication is implemented, and leaves queued question handling as an explicit learner task.

nodes.name: health
nodes.summary: Reports the bot skeleton as not ready and its Slack transport as unconfigured.

nodes.name: slack_events
nodes.summary: Rejects all Slack event requests with HTTP 501 until a selected adapter and authentication checks are implemented and tested.

nodes.name: handle_question
nodes.summary: Defines the asynchronous question-handling seam for the future deduplicated queue, bounded read-only tools, audit trail, and separately approved mutations.

nodes.name: requirements.in
nodes.summary: Declares the minimal direct Python dependencies for the fail-closed ChatOps skeleton: pinned FastAPI and Uvicorn with standard extras. A Slack SDK is intentionally deferred until the transport is selected.

nodes.name: requirements.txt
nodes.summary: Locks the complete ChatOps Python dependency graph with exact versions and hashes for reproducible container installation. It is the generated install input consumed by the bot Docker image.

nodes.name: antigravity-rule.md
nodes.summary: Instructs Antigravity agents to read the root project context before each task, treat tool and RAG outputs as untrusted, and report the constraints, diff, and tests used. It avoids duplicating the canonical AGENTS.md content.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Documents the Day 2 read-only InsightHub MCP server, including SDK protocol modes, bounded tools, environment policy, host configuration, threat boundaries, and verification commands. It records the intended fail-closed contract for API and Prometheus access through stdio.

nodes.name: host-config.mjs
nodes.summary: Generates machine-specific MCP host configuration for Claude, Codex, or Antigravity without modifying host files. It emits absolute server paths, conservative loopback defaults, a read-only tool allowlist, and bounded request limits.

nodes.name: manifest.json
nodes.summary: Defines the versioned MCP starter contract: installation and verification commands, protocol versions, exposed tools, fixed endpoints, resource limits, and explicit read-only scope. It also records fixture and live smoke-test expectations.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Configures the private ESM MCP package, Node 22 runtime floor, unit and smoke scripts, and pinned modern and legacy SDK dependencies used for compatibility verification.

nodes.name: smoke.mjs
nodes.summary: Runs the MCP end-to-end smoke workflow against either a deterministic loopback fixture or a live InsightHub API. It exercises modern, auto-negotiated, legacy, and SDK v1 clients while checking tool discovery, calls, wire protocol observations, and secret-canary non-disclosure.

nodes.name: core.mjs
nodes.summary: Implements the security-critical read-only MCP service core: strict loopback configuration, bounded HTTP GETs, concurrency and cancellation control, response schema validation, and privacy-preserving projections for health, documents, and fixed Prometheus queries.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses fail-closed validation, fixed route/query maps, absolute deadlines, and output projection rather than heuristic secret filtering.

nodes.name: SafeError
nodes.summary: Carries a controlled error code that can safely cross the MCP service boundary without exposing raw provider or caller data.

nodes.name: loopbackOrigin
nodes.summary: Validates an HTTP origin against the exact IPv4, IPv6, or localhost loopback forms and rejects paths, credentials, fragments, and invalid ports to prevent SSRF.

nodes.name: readConfig
nodes.summary: Parses and freezes MCP environment configuration, enforcing exact tool names, deny-all semantics, Prometheus gating, loopback-only origins, and hard timeout and response-size caps.

nodes.name: getJson
nodes.summary: Performs a bounded, cancellable GET to one of the fixed local API or Prometheus routes and rejects redirects, oversized headers or bodies, compression, wrong content types, timeouts, and malformed JSON.

nodes.name: createService
nodes.summary: Creates the bounded tool dispatcher that enforces the server allowlist and concurrency limit, calls fixed upstream routes, validates response schemas, and returns minimal structured projections without sensitive metadata.

nodes.name: server.mjs
nodes.summary: Bootstraps the stdio MCP server, registers only enabled read-only tools with strict Zod schemas, and maps internal failures to stable non-reflective errors. The process rejects unexpected arguments and supports graceful SIGINT and SIGTERM shutdown.

nodes.name: buildServer
nodes.summary: Constructs an MCP server and registers each configured tool with its strict input schema, read-only annotations, service handler, and controlled error response.

nodes.name: client.mjs
nodes.summary: Provides a reusable test client that launches the real stdio server with either modern or legacy MCP SDK transports. It captures bounded stderr and both directions of the JSON-RPC wire exchange for protocol assertions.

nodes.name: connectClient
nodes.summary: Starts and connects a selected modern or legacy SDK client to the real MCP child process while recording inbound and outbound messages and bounded stderr.

nodes.name: core.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Tests the MCP core's fail-closed controls, including SSRF rejection, allowlists, fixed routes and Prometheus queries, metadata projection, response limits, timeout behavior, cancellation, concurrency, and canary non-disclosure.

nodes.name: fixture.mjs
nodes.summary: Creates a deterministic loopback HTTP fixture that emulates InsightHub health, readiness, documents, and Prometheus endpoints while embedding a labeled secret canary in data that the MCP layer must remove.

nodes.name: fixture
nodes.summary: Starts an ephemeral loopback server with default endpoint responses or a caller-supplied handler, records requests, and returns a deterministic asynchronous cleanup function.

nodes.name: server.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Exercises the real MCP stdio server with modern and legacy clients, proving that direct protocol calls cannot bypass allowlists or strict schemas and that startup errors do not reflect credentials. It also verifies deny-all operation and bounded document and Prometheus inputs.

nodes.name: denied
nodes.summary: Sends a raw tools/call request around the client's local schema cache and asserts that the server or MCP protocol rejects the operation.

tour.title: Project And Learning Arc
tour.description: Begin with the repository overview and authoritative student specification to understand InsightHub as both a working RAG notebook and a seven-day DevOps learning project. The starter deliberately begins with three synchronous services, while the curriculum progressively adds asynchronous ingestion, tooling, infrastructure, observability, ChatOps, and governance.

tour.title: API Bootstrap
tour.description: The FastAPI entry point assembles database lifecycle management, bounded middleware, metrics, error handling, and the public routers described in the overview. Reading it establishes the runtime boundary of the current synchronous backend before following individual request paths.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI lifespan functions centralize startup and shutdown resources, while middleware wraps every request to enforce cross-cutting behavior such as metrics and sanitized failure handling.

tour.title: Configuration And Readiness
tour.description: Building on the bootstrap, immutable settings select fixture or real providers and derive the embedding identity that must remain stable for an index. Database initialization then creates the shared connection pool and refuses readiness when schema or embedding-identity checks fail, keeping configuration mistakes out of normal request handling.
tour.languageLesson: A cached immutable settings object gives Python services one validated configuration snapshot, avoiding inconsistent environment reads across requests.

tour.title: Vector Data Contract
tour.description: The database schema turns the configuration rules into durable invariants: one embedding identity, lifecycle-aware documents, and ordered vectorized chunks. Foreign keys and check constraints ensure that only ready documents with compatible embeddings participate in retrieval, while the HNSW index makes cosine search practical.
tour.languageLesson: PostgreSQL constraints enforce lifecycle and identity rules independently of application code; pgvector's HNSW index accelerates approximate nearest-neighbor search over embeddings.

tour.title: Synchronous Upload Path
tour.description: The document router is the current write-side API: it validates an upload, persists it, runs ingestion inline, and returns HTTP 201 only after the document is ready. This synchronous contract is the baseline that Day 1 intentionally replaces with queue acceptance and HTTP 202 while preserving listing, deletion, and controlled errors.

tour.title: Chunk And Embed Pipeline
tour.description: Inside ingestion, extracted text becomes overlapping chunks and then deterministic fixture vectors or real-provider embeddings in bounded batches. Strict count, dimension, finiteness, norm, and identity validation protects the storage contract from malformed or incompatible provider output before chunks are committed atomically.

tour.title: Retrieval And Generation
tour.description: The read-side RAG path embeds the user's question, searches ready chunks within the active embedding identity, and passes bounded context to a provider adapter. The chat router joins retrieval and generation into a provenance-rich response with sources, contexts, latency, model identity, mode, and token usage.

tour.title: Web Experience
tour.description: The Next.js home page presents the upload and chat workflow while loading initial document state on the server and degrading gracefully when FastAPI is unavailable. Its bounded proxy is the browser-facing safety boundary, allowing only known upload and chat targets while enforcing payload limits, timeouts, and normalized errors.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js App Router can combine server-rendered pages for initial data with route handlers that keep backend URLs, validation, and failure translation on the server side.

tour.title: Day One Async Target
tour.description: With the synchronous path understood, the ingestion-worker contract defines the intended Day 1 split: the API stores a pending document, enqueues work through Redis and ARQ, and returns HTTP 202 immediately. A separate worker must drive pending documents to ready or failed without duplicating chunks on retry, while leaving the chat contract compatible with ready data.

tour.title: Local Service Topology
tour.description: Docker Compose turns the code paths into the runnable local starter by connecting PostgreSQL/pgvector, FastAPI, and Next.js, with an optional Ollama profile and persistent volumes. The service Dockerfiles produce non-root, health-checked images, and the Makefile exposes a stable command surface for lifecycle and verification tasks.
tour.languageLesson: Compose health checks and named volumes make service readiness and persistent state explicit; multi-stage Docker builds separate dependency installation and compilation from smaller non-root runtime images.

tour.title: Contracts And Verification
tour.description: The integration suite exercises the real API, PostgreSQL, pgvector, retries, identity conflicts, retrieval, and sanitized failures established in earlier steps. The central verifier expands those checks into stable PASS, FAILED, or INCOMPLETE outcomes for the starter and every lab day, making executable evidence—not documentation alone—the final contract.
